When scavenging, new leatherbacks will take bites, but it is not a behavior seen with live prey outside of very rare occasions. It is worth noting that the new leatherback's bite is more than strong enough to break metahuman bones and is quite dangerous. It is not, however, its primary defense mechanism—for that, they rely upon their magical ability to compel animals to swim as deep as they can. Against aquatic predators, this gives the turtle plenty of time to escape, but against non-aquatic predators or interlopers, this can be quite dangerous indeed.
